answer: The design leans on time-locked work history, capped per identity per epoch, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Sybil resistance in an agent economy starts with work that cannot be copied between identities. The cedar of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. The atlas holds work receipts rather than names, so the whisper of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread.
